title: PharmEasy Health Report 2025
purpose: Learn India's health and wellness industry for a report that uncovers an insight.
about: What India bought to stay healthy in 2025: the trends and numbers that matter for a health and wellness report.

sections.title: What India bought to stay healthy

questions.prompt: What two big shifts does the report say Indian health buying made in 2025?

keyPoints.text: From acute / episodic (sick) care to preventive, proactive care
From metro-led demand to Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities

questions.answer:
(1) **Acute → preventive:** vitamins, supplements, diagnostics and chronic-care management became year-round habits rather than things bought when sick. (2) **Metro → Tier-2/3:** smaller cities drove a growing share of the growth.

The report's own one-liner: a move "from reactive panic to proactive wellness".

questions.prompt: What was PharmEasy's most-ordered category of the year, which single product was bought most, and how much did that product grow?
questions.answer: **Vitamins & supplements** had the highest order volumes of any category; multivitamins top the monthly chart. The single most-purchased product was **Vitamin B supplements, up 33% vs 2024**, across cities and age groups. Calcium came a close second; Vitamin D was also among the top national purchases.

questions.prompt: Diagnostics: which test was booked most, which two tests rose especially in Tier-2 cities, and what changed about tests like CBC and lipid profiles?

keyPoints.text: Rising in Tier-2: thyroid panels and HbA1c (diabetes)
CBC / lipid became routine tracking, not illness-led testing

questions.answer:
**Vitamin D tests** were the most-booked. **Thyroid panels and HbA1c** rose, especially in Tier-2 cities. **CBC and lipid profiles** moved from "test when ill" to regular tracking.

This is the diagnostics side of the same preventive shift: people testing to monitor, not to diagnose.

questions.prompt: Blood pressure and diabetes medicines made up what share of chronic-condition orders?
questions.answer: **93%** of chronic-condition orders. Thyroid medicines were smaller but stable, especially among urban women; **women were nearly 60% of thyroid testing** (Delhi NCR and Bengaluru led). 71% is the weekday share of all orders, a different stat.

questions.prompt: GLP-1 medicines were flagged as a newly emerging category. How fast did they grow, and who is using them?

keyPoints.text: Nearly half of users are 25–45 (notable share 25–35)

questions.answer:
**~12% average month-on-month growth**, consistent through the year, with uptake varying by city. **Nearly half of GLP-1 users are aged 25–45**, with a notable share aged 25–35.

The report reads this as early engagement by young adults, not only older diabetic patients.

questions.prompt: Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities: name categories where they grew faster, and the products first-time buyers started with.

keyPoints.text: Faster growth (any 2): vitamins, sexual wellness, diagnostics, fitness
First-time buyer entry (any 1): multivitamins, speciality supplements, glucometer strips, sunscreens, moisturisers

questions.answer:
Tier-2/3 grew faster in **vitamins, sexual wellness, diagnostics and fitness**. First-time buyers came in mainly through **multivitamins, speciality supplements, glucometer strips, sunscreens and moisturisers**, so wellness and self-care products, not prescriptions, are the entry point.

Also: Tier-2 cities placed 22% more "SOS-style" orders. The article doesn't say what that's compared with, so don't lean on it without the original report.

questions.prompt: What does the timing of orders (weekday vs weekend, morning, late night) suggest about how people use an online pharmacy?

keyPoints.text: Mostly planned / routine restocking and chronic care, not emergencies

questions.answer:
**Weekdays made up 71% of orders.** Mornings (6–9 am) are routine restocking of vitamins, calcium and daily-use medicines. Even late night (10 pm–4 am) is **chronic care, not emergencies**: blood thinners top it. Weekends bring spikes in antacids, skincare, sun care and exploratory OTC buys (Sunday antacids run 14–18% higher).

Takeaway: the channel is used for planned replenishment more than urgent need.

questions.prompt: The report says “every second household” did what at least once in the year?
questions.answer: **Bought a digestive product.** Gut health is a mass category: Hyderabad is called a gut-health hub (antacids, probiotics), Delhi and Bengaluru also show strong gut-care demand, and antacids spike on weekends. Note this is among PharmEasy's customers, not all Indian households.

questions.prompt: Which OTC and self-care categories does the report call out as rising? Name at least two.

keyPoints.text: Homeopathy, one of the fastest-growing categories
Protein powders & fitness supplements (Gurgaon, Mumbai lead whey; Tier-2 catching up)

questions.answer: **Homeopathy** was one of the fastest-growing categories. **Protein powders and fitness supplements** surged (Gurgaon and Mumbai lead whey protein; Tier-2 is catching up). **Home-monitoring devices** (thermometers, glucometers, oximeters) saw steady demand, peaking at seasonal transitions.

questions.prompt: What does the report's data actually cover?
options: A nationally representative survey of Indian households
Anonymised PharmEasy medicine, lab and wellness orders, 1 Jan – 20 Nov 2025
Retail pharmacy sales audited across online and offline channels
questions.answer:
**Only orders placed on PharmEasy**, 1 January to 20 November 2025, and the report says it doesn't aim to show broader national or regional trends.

For your report: treat these as signals from online, platform users (my read: likely urban and already health-aware), and look for an independent source before calling anything a national trend.
